record.original_question: Let {alpha_k}_{k>=0} and {beta_k}_{k>=0} be multiplier sequences of nonnegative real numbers. Characterize all functions Psi:R x R -> R such that the pointwise transformed sequence {Psi(alpha_k,beta_k)}_{k>=0} is again a multiplier sequence.

evidence.quote: Problem 24. Let {alpha_k}_0^infinity and {beta_k}_0^infinity be multiplier sequences of non-negative real numbers. Characterize all functions Psi : R x R -> R such that {Psi(alpha_k, beta_k)}_0^infinity is again a multiplier sequence.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A sequence $\{\gamma_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ of real numbers is called a multiplier sequence if, for every real polynomial $p(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n} a_k x^k$ all of whose zeros are real, the polynomial $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \gamma_k a_k x^k$ also has only real zeros.

Let $\{\alpha_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ and $\{\beta_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ be multiplier sequences consisting of nonnegative real numbers. Characterize all functions $\Psi : \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with the property that, for every such pair of nonnegative multiplier sequences $\{\alpha_k\}$ and $\{\beta_k\}$, the pointwise transformed sequence $\{\Psi(\alpha_k,\beta_k)\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is again a multiplier sequence.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published characterization of all binary functions Ψ that send pairs of nonnegative multiplier sequences to multiplier sequences. The problem is posed as an open problem in the literature on multiplier sequences and no resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Pointwise Multiplication - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: General references on pointwise operations; no characterization of Ψ for multiplier sequences found.
status_evidence.claim: No source providing a complete characterization was located.
